newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: New French govt could slow bank consolidation - ABN.
newsitem.headline: New French govt could slow bank consolidation - ABN.

text.p: Jan Kalff, chairman of the managing board of Dutch bank ABN Amro said Sunday's election victory by the French Socialists could slow down the required consolidation of France's banking sector and affect plans to privatise banks.
Kalff told a briefing at the International Monetary Conference (IMC) that it was highly likely that the new government would be more resistant to any consolidation that leads to layoffs.

Kalff said there was enormous overcapacity in the French banking market and "certainly an overbranched situation if not an overbanked situation that can only be solved by a great deal more consolidation, reduction in the number of branches and that is going to create new unemployment," Kalff said.
"It is highly likely that the new government will be more resistant to unemployment measures taken by banks," he added.
Kalff said the former centre-right government seemed to have reluctantly prepared to accept this consequence.
"I don't know what the new government will do, but in that respect it could indeed have a negative effect on consolidation in France," Kalff said.
He added it might also have an effect on the plans to privatise French banks.
